newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nichiboshin to post 47.95 bln yen special loss.
newsitem.headline: Nichiboshin to post 47.95 bln yen special loss.

text.p: Japanese financial institution Nichiboshin Ltd said on Friday it would post an extraordinary loss of 47.95 billion yen for the first half of fiscal 1996/97.
The extraordinary loss for the six months to September 30 includes 34.30 billion yen in loan loss provisions for a financially strapped non-bank subsidiary, the company said in a statement.
As a result, the company now expects a parent net loss for the first half of 48.71 billion yen. It had earlier projected a parent net profit of 5.3 billion yen.
Nichiboshin said the loan loss provision was made earlier than expected. The company had expected to make such a provision in the second half, it said.
However, the company said that it would not revise its earnings forecast for fiscal 1996/97, ending next March, because it expects all creditors will agree on its five-year restructuring programme.

In May, it projected a parent net profit of 16.8 billion yen for 1996/97 and nil parent current profit. In 1995/96, the company posted a parent current loss of 42.91 billion yen and a parent net loss of 32.63 billion.

The company said that while some of the more than 100 creditors had yet to agree with the non-bank on its restructuring programme, the company would continue to make efforts to gain their approval in the second half.
Under the programme, creditors were asked to forgive a portion of their loans to Nichiboshin.
Nichiboshin's borrowings from financial institutions total some 900 billion yen. The company wants lenders to forgive about 500 billion yen worth of loans in the five-year restructuring period.
